subject: Define acceptance guardrails & test rundown for NovaProspect evaluation
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@novaprospect.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask: acceptance definition for our 6-week evaluation

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the observability hooks. We need to lock down acceptance criteria so our internal stakeholders (engineering, security, procurement) can sign off and unblock the pilot kickoff next Monday. High level asks from our side: clear pass/fail signal for the evaluation, a short list of acceptance tests we can run, and an agreed stoplight for go/no-go decisions at weeks 2, 4, and 6.

Key constraints:
- We must validate performance against our production-like traffic (peak ~250 req/s, avg 40 req/s).
- We need evidence of data isolation and logs for auditing.
- Procurement needs a clear cutover checklist for contract acceptance and SOC2 artifacts.

Can you share a one-page test rundown + exit gates spreadsheet and owners by EOD? Procurement will be cc'd on follow-ups.

Attachments: none (we'll upload the initial MAP once you send it).

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Park
Director, Integrations 
NovaProspect

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: acceptance definition for our 6-week evaluation

Hi Emily — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise MAP + acceptance rundown (MAP_NovaProspect_v1.xlsx). Below is the proposed acceptance guardrail set and the exit gates we recommend for each decision point. This is intentionally tight so your teams can run focused tests and we can measure objectively.

Summary acceptance categories (pass threshold / test owner):
1) Functional correctness (intent match / safety): >92% intent-match on the sampled prompt set; zero critical safety incidents. Owner: NP engineering + Redwood success (Marissa).
2) Latency & throughput: P95 tail latency <300ms at target load (40 req/s sustained), no more than 10% error rate under peak 250 req/s. Owner: Redwood infra (Vivek) + NP perf lead.
3) Cost per active session: tokenized cost projection within 20% of the QPS model in the MAP. Owner: Lukas.
4) Observability & auditability: request/response logs, token-level cost traces, and KV cache metrics available in Redwood Console; evidence export for auditors. Owner: NP security + Redwood support.
5) Integration resilience: automatic fallback to a distilled model variant on overload and documented rollback steps. Owner: NP SRE + Redwood.

Exit gates (week checkpoints):
- Week 2 (smoke gate): sanity checks only. If Functional correctness <80% or errors >15% at smoke load => stop and remediate.
- Week 4 (hard gate): all critical integrations live; if Latency/Throughput or Observability fail => remediation sprint (7 days) then re-test.
- Week 6 (go/no-go): all acceptance categories must meet thresholds. Single critical safety incident or systemic data isolation failure => fail to go-live.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Test A (intent match): 500 labeled prompts across key intents, blind scoring. Pass if >=92% match.
- Test B (throughput): incremental load test to peak for 1 hour; monitor p95/p99, error rates, and fallback triggers.
- Test C (audit trace): run sample flows and extract full request/response trace; validate KMS access and absence of PII in logs per contract.
- Test D (fallback & rollback): simulate model variant failure and validate automatic fallback completes within 3s and no user-facing errors.

Evidence & artifacts to collect: scorecards, perf graphs (p50/p95/p99), sample traces (anonymized), MAP worksheet with run dates and owners, signed checklist from NP procurement for SOC2 references.

Next steps:
1) Confirm owners above and add NP procurement contact (procurement@novaprospect.com).
2) We'll share the MAP spreadsheet (attached) and a lightweight runbook for test execution.
3) Set 30-min alignment on Thursday to finalize checklist.

Attachment: MAP_NovaProspect_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-MAP-NovaProspect

Emily — quick additions from contract/ops perspective:

1) Evidence checklist: procurement needs a one-line mapping from each acceptance test to an artifact type (e.g., "Test A -> Labeled scoring CSV + scorer notes"). We'll include a DocuSign-ready signoff page for the week-6 acceptance so legal can attach the conditional cutover clause.
2) SOC2 items: we'll attach the SOC2 snapshot and a short statement on retention / encryption. If NP needs an SOC2 bridge letter, add that as an item in the MAP under "deliverables".
3) Acceptance owners need explicit emails in the MAP (not just names). Lukas — please add NP perf lead and NP SRE emails.

Proposed timeline tweak: move the week-4 hard gate to day 26 (so there's a 10-day buffer for remediation before the final week-6 decision). If that works for NP, we'll update the MAP and schedule remediation windows.

Thanks — I've added a procurement checklist tab to the attached MAP (same spreadsheet).

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
